data.name: Radial Impact
data.detailed_description:
Radial Impact Available Through Unreal Engine 4

You can find Radial Impact available through the Learning Tab of the Unreal Engine 4 Launcher for free download so that you can learn how I made the game!


Acerca do jogo

Radial Impact is a fast-paced, single-player game that challenges players’ reflexes by matching the sizes of two circles; one static and one dynamic.

Game Features:

Single-Player.
Multiple Game Modes (Classic, Time Trial, and Waves).
Simple Mechanics (Click to Interact).
Dynamic Circle Sizes and Locations.
Developed solely by Devin Sherry.

Classic Mode – Overview

Game-play focused on getting the highest score.
Points earned based on how close the player matches the shape of the circles.
Three Lives – Once all lives are lost, the player loses and the game ends.
Slow-down ability unlocked if the player gets a Perfect rating 5x in a row.
If the player reaches a 10X Perfect multiplier, they earn back a life if one was lost.
Lives are lost if the player gets either a Bad or a Miss rating.
Saved Data for High Score.



Time Trial – Overview

Game-play focused on lasting the longest without time running out.
Time is added and subtracted based on how close the player matches the shape of the circles.
The player starts with 59 seconds until the game ends.
Slow-down ability unlocked if the player gets a Perfect rating 5x in a row.
Saved Data for Longest Time.



Waves Mode – Overview

The goal of the player is to earn a score that is larger than the “Score to Beat” for each waves option and set there own high score.
There are multiple “Waves” options for the player to choose from. There are 5 Waves, 10 Waves, 25 Waves, and 50 Waves.
A “Wave” consists of one turn of the player matching the two circles shapes.
At the start, only the “5 Waves” mode is unlocked for the player. As the player scores higher than the “Score to Beat” the player will unlock the higher waves options.
Slow-down ability unlocked if the player gets a Perfect rating 5x in a row.
Saved Data to track which waves options have been unlocked.

reviews.review:
[h1] Overview [/h1] 

Radial Impact is described from their store page  as "a fast-paced, single-player game that challenges players' reflexes by matching the sizes of two circles; one static and one dynamic" and to its credit it gets half of that right. However, Radial Impact is neither challenging nor fast-paced. In fact, I'd wager this could sparsely be called a game at all. 

Your given three options from the title screen: time trials, "classic" mode and waves. Between the three of them you essentially do the same thing: you'll be given two circles, and one will come inward or outward and you're tasked with clicking inside the smaller of the two when they perfectly overlap. In time trials, you're timed, in classic you go until it becomes as exhilarating as watching paint dry and in waves you select between 5-50 waves of one circle each.  At the end of whatever mode you've playing you'll be given a score. That's it. There is no leaderboard  [nobody plays it even if there was] and the game doesn't even track your own high score, as it resets to default after each run.   

Why any of this amounts to a saleable product eludes me, as Radial Impact is a perfect example of minimal effort and lack of innovation. There is no end goal, no purpose, no achievements or even a reason you're clicking other than because the game requires you to do so. 

Everything about this game is poorly done. The background is dull with static animation and obnoxious color changing effects. The juxtaposition of the music and game speed make zero sense, often being at opposite sides of the spectrum in terms of speed. The content, if you can even call it that, is practically nonexistent. I cannot even begin to fathom why this game was made. You'd probably find my enjoyment in taking the $1.00 and burning it, than adding this game to your playlist. 

[h1] Pros [/h1] 

[list]
[*] There are absolutely zero pros about playing this game.
[/list]

[h1] Cons [/h1] 
[list] 
[*] Left click to win. That's all you do. Forever.
[*] The pace of the music conflicts with the pace of the "game".
[*] Zero playability and even less replayability. 
[/list]

Overall, Radial Impact is a poor excuse for a game. There are no positives to be found, no joy to be had and no effort to be seen. Chalk this game up to one you can easily ignore. Don't waste your time or your money on it.
